questionText: Two cars start at the same time from the same location and go in the same direction. The speed of the first car is $50$ km/h and the speed of the second car is $60$ km/h. The number of hours it takes for the distance between the two cars to be $20$ km is ___.
explanation:
Given:
Speed of the first car, $S_1 = 50$ km/h
Speed of the second car, $S_2 = 60$ km/h

Since both cars start from the same location and travel in the same direction, we can calculate their relative speed by taking the difference of their individual speeds.
Relative Speed $= S_2 - S_1 = 60 - 50 = 10$ km/h.

The target distance between the two cars is given as $20$ km.

Using the formula for time:
$\text{Time} = \frac{\text{Distance}}{\text{Relative Speed}}$

$\text{Time} = \frac{20}{10} = 2$ hours.

Therefore, it will take $2$ hours for the distance between the two cars to be $20$ km.
